sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Gordion
sources.note: Direct description and Outstanding Universal Value read: Iron Age kingdom, monumental gate, coloured pebble mosaics, timber engineering and royal tumuli. The imported 1500 BCE start is not an attested kingdom founding.

sources.title: Penn Museum, Digital Gordion: Iron Age Gordion
sources.note: Direct full excavation synthesis read. Early Iron Age and Early/Middle Phrygian phases; later-eighth-century Midas; residential hearths/ovens/storage; common cemetery. Proposed migrant identity and worker slavery not presented as settled. Precise late Midas death stories explicitly rejected by source.

sources.title: Gareth Darbyshire and Gabriel Pizzorno, Gordion in History, Expedition (2009)
sources.note: Direct full article read: late-eighth-century Midas/Mita in Assyrian records, sixth-century Lydian dominance followed by Persian conquest and district-centre role; Gordion occupation predates Phrygian state. Outdated blanket phrase still not deciphered is not adopted for Phrygian language.

sources.title: Penn Museum, Digital Gordion: Textile Production at Gordion
sources.note: Direct specialist account read: twelve excavated workshop units, cooking installations/grinding platforms, more than one thousand inventoried spindle whorls, warp-weighted looms. Organizational interpretation distinguished from unknown worker status.

sources.title: Penn Museum, Gordion Furniture Project
sources.note: Direct project report read: Tumulus W/P/MM, wood species and preservation, secure early lathe evidence from W plates, funerary residue analysis interpreted as meat/legume stew and mixed fermented drink. Early claim that this is Midas himself corrected with revised chronology; no royal menu universalized.

sources.title: Penn Museum, The Funeral in Tumulus MM
sources.note: Direct archaeological interpretation read: log coffin with dyed textiles, fourteen furniture pieces, three large cauldrons about 150 litres each, animal-headed vessels and serving arrangement. Identity not claimed as securely Midas or Gordias.

sources.title: Penn Museum Archives, Gordion Excavation Records: Horse Trappings/Tumulus P Quadriga
sources.note: Original institutional finding aid read: section Horse Trappings/Tumulus P Quadriga, Ellen Kohler research, small toy quadriga in child burial. Does not prove every child owned toys or identify biological relatives.

sources.title: Penn Museum, Digital Gordion: Chronology
sources.note: Direct New Chronology section read, especially seed radiocarbon and tomb timber dates. Tumulus MM ca.740 BCE predates Midas still active709 BCE. URL already used by cimerians; final cumulative budget includes its passage and conservatively its override summary.

proposedOverrides.name: Phrygians
proposedOverrides.summary: Phrygian communities developed an influential Iron Age kingdom centred on Gordion, renowned for monumental building and skilled crafts.

batchIdentityNotes.identity: Imported culture record, treated as Phrygian communities with an Iron Age kingdom centred on Gordion; neither a 1500 BCE empire nor all earlier occupants of Anatolia.
batchIdentityNotes.overlap: No additional Phrygia ID found in imported civilizations index; exact ID absent from overrides, runtime cards and staged bundles at inspection. Cimmerian card discusses separate Gordion chronology evidence but is not a duplicate polity.
batchIdentityNotes.mapEvidence: Three identical polygons, world-bc1500/world-bc1000/world-bc700, bounds 27.5817-35.6782 E and36.0779-42.0433 N. Outline much broader than securely traced changing political control. Public opening warns map coverage is not kingdom lifetime.
batchIdentityNotes.chronology: Approximate Early Phrygian phase950-800, Midas late eighth century, later Lydian/Persian control. Old ca.700 fire/Midas tomb identifications not adopted. Scholarly Midas Monument sixth-century date distinguished from eighth-century king. Roman writing placed in later-continuity passage.
batchIdentityNotes.limits: No evidence-backed general school curriculum, medical care or toilet system located in bounded research; no filler claims. Child burial is privileged, royal banquet is exceptional, workers status remains unspecified. Shared chronology URL cumulatively checked against runtime cimerians card.
